note: Stage one, draft 1 (9:2–9:21). Four verses: two majors, both taken (9:4 the gerund's accusative, with the future passive inside the same remark; 9:8b 'para o juízo'); two minors refused under the glossary (9:6 the singular 'século do século', 9:10 'auxiliador'). Marks confirmed in all 21 verses. Passed without remark: 'fizestes valer o meu juízo', 'julgais a justiça', 'Repreendestes', 'desfaleceram até o fim', 'o orbe da terra', 'pedindo contas do sangue', 'ficaram cravadas', 'ficou preso', 'executando juízos', 'Voltem … para o inferno', 'não se fortaleça', 'à vossa vista', 'um legislador'.

outcomes.remark: the active gerund has inimícum meum as its OBJECT: it is making the enemy turn back; 'Ao voltar para trás o meu inimigo' makes him the subject (MAJOR) → 'Ao fazer voltar para trás o meu inimigo'
outcomes.reason: Right on the Latin's grammar; 'fazer voltar' still names no agent.

outcomes.remark: infirmabúntur is passive → 'serão enfraquecidos'
outcomes.reason: Voice is kept (the brief). Cost: the colon is five syllables over.

outcomes.remark: 'pelos séculos dos séculos' pluralises the Latin's singular → 'pelo século do século' (minor)
outcomes.reason: The glossary formula (asked and refused the same way at 118:44); the singular is not said in Portuguese prayer, and both Vulgate-family versions have the plural.

outcomes.remark: 'in judício' places the preparing in judgment; 'para o juízo' introduces a purpose (MAJOR) → 'em juízo'
outcomes.reason: Right: the preposition was interpreted. The court sense of 'em juízo' is the verse's own.

outcomes.remark: adjútor names the one who helps; 'auxílio' is a defensible metonymy → 'auxiliador' (minor)
outcomes.reason: The glossary row adjútor → auxílio (Ps 117:6–7; 118:114 held against three readings), the same metonymy as suscéptor → amparo; 'auxiliador' is long and rare.

note: Stage one, draft 1. Eight verses; best 9:7b, worst 9:19. 'O salmo tem sobriedade e uma voz de oração reconhecível, com imagens fortes e boas terminações … a repetição de «até o fim» deve permanecer, pois pertence ao próprio latim.' Five taken (9:3, 9:13, 9:14, 9:17 whole or nearly; 9:16a and 9:19 by order with the Latin's verb kept), one overtaken by the Latinist (9:4), one refused and kept as an option (9:6).

outcomes.remark: the vocative parts the singing from its object → 'Altíssimo, entoarei salmos ao vosso nome'
outcomes.reason: Order only (D2).

outcomes.remark: the subject comes late after 'voltar para trás' → 'Quando o meu inimigo voltar para trás'
outcomes.reason: Overtaken by the Latinist's major: the enemy is the gerund's object, not the subject; 'Ao fazer voltar' has no late subject to wait for.

outcomes.remark: 'séculos' ends the verse proparoxytone → 'pelos séculos dos séculos, e para sempre'
outcomes.reason: It reverses the Latin's two members; the Latin ends on the proparoxytone sǽculi too; formulas stay whole.

outcomes.remark: the intercalated clause holds back the main verb, which has no expressed subject → 'Porque, ao pedir contas do sangue deles, ele se lembrou'
outcomes.reason: Grammar and a named subject (D2).

outcomes.remark: 'humilhação vinda' is clipped written prose → 'a humilhação que me vem dos meus inimigos'
outcomes.reason: A clause for the participle, as Douay-Rheims; 'a minha' kept for meam.

outcomes.remark: the inversion holds back the subject, and 'fazer uma destruição' is an unusual pairing → 'as nações ficaram cravadas na destruição que causaram'
outcomes.reason: The order is taken; 'causaram' is refused — fecérunt is fácere, and the oddness is the Latin's. Kept as an option.

outcomes.remark: the bare gerund after 'será conhecido' leaves the tie loose → 'ao executar juízos'
outcomes.reason: Grammar (D2).

outcomes.remark: 'não será até o fim' hangs until the abstract subject; carried-over order (WORST LINE) → 'Porque o esquecimento do pobre não durará até o fim'
outcomes.reason: The order is taken; 'durará' for erit is refused (more than a supplied copula) and kept as an option.

note: Stage one, draft 1, Portuguese only. 28 items, 3 unknown words (orbe, equidade, desígnios). Almost everything is the Latin's own range heard as the Latin is read: whose name, cities and memory (deles), the enemy as a host (plural verbs), whose blood (9:13), 'filha de Sião' heard as a woman, homo as 'the male'. The legal readings were heard right first: 9:5 'the Lord gave the speaker right', 9:13 'the Lord calls the victims' death to account', 9:17 'applying sentences'. No change made on its account; 9:4 changed for the Latinist.

outcomes.remark: 'fizestes valer o meu juízo': made my opinion prevail / made good the judgment on my cause
outcomes.reason: The right reading was heard first ('O Senhor deu razão a quem fala'); the verb is there to make it so.

outcomes.remark: 'julgais a justiça': judge justice itself / judge causes justly
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own oddness; the right sense was heard first.

outcomes.remark: 'deles': the poor / the nations / other victims
outcomes.reason: The Latin's eórum is as open; the listener settles on the poor by the verse's end, as a Latin reader does.

outcomes.remark: 'a filha de Sião' can sound like a woman; the city is not explained
outcomes.reason: The Latin's image (rule 5); no footnote in the text.

outcomes.remark: 'Voltem … para o inferno' suggests a return to a place they had been
outcomes.reason: The Greek's verb is 'turn back' (ἀποστρέφω, as in 9:4 εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω), and the psalm ties the two verses; the likely hearing was 'be sent to hell'.

outcomes.remark: 'não perecerá até o fim': will not be lost for ever / will last until the end and may end then
outcomes.reason: The Latin's in finem is as open; kept apart from in ætérnum. Evidence recorded on the glossary row.

outcomes.remark: 'o homem': humankind / one man / males
outcomes.reason: homo; the right sense heard first.

outcomes.remark: unknown word 'orbe'
outcomes.reason: Kept as the glossary proposal ('o mundo' is the retreat); recorded on the new open row for the main session.

outcomes.remark: unknown word 'equidade'
outcomes.reason: Glossary (ǽquitas → equidade, working); the Ps 118 blind reader listed it too.

outcomes.remark: unknown word 'desígnios' (yet heard as 'the Lord's plans')
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; kept.

note: Stage one, draft 2 (revise_v2.py; draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json). Latinist: 9:4 'Ao fazer voltar para trás o meu inimigo: * serão enfraquecidos', 9:8b 'em juízo'. Stylist: 9:3 vocative first, 9:13 'ao pedir … ele se lembrou', 9:14 'que me vem dos meus inimigos', 9:16a subject first, 9:17 'ao executar juízos', 9:19 subject first with 'será'. New decisions infirmabuntur and v19a; saeculi now takes the whole phrase so that the stylist's reversal can be shown. Checks (partial.py): hard pass; new soft flags 9:4b +5 (the passive; accepted) and 9:17a +4; no rhyme flag, though 9:19 now ends both cola on 'fim' — the Latin's repetition.
